children: Swedish consumer confidence fell sharply in October to 94.3 points, from a marginally revised 102.3 points in September, data from the National Institute of Economic Research (NIER) showed on Thursday.
Overall sentiment, which also includes industry, construction and retailers, rose to 108.1 points compared to revised 107.2 points a month earlier.
Expectations for households' own finances and the Swedish economy over the next 12 months drove the decline in consumer confidence, NIER said
Consumer confidence returned to June levels, with households' financial outlook now clearly below normal, it said
At the same time, manufacturing confidence rose to its highest level since August 2022, supported by stronger production plans than in September and improved order-book assessments
Businesses' pricing plans strengthened from September, indicating price increases to a greater extent than normal
